item.title: [karpathy]One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

[BossMon_02]The next evolution of artificial intelligence will not be defined only by larger models but by who has access to them. Decentralized AI removes barriers that often limit participation in innovation. Developers, researchers, and everyday users can all contribute to building smarter systems. This creates an ecosystem where progress is driven by the community instead of a single authority.
Blockchain brings trust to AI by making important activities transparent and verifiable @TheARCTERMINAL . Contributions, rewards, and governance decisions can all be recorded on chain. This reduces uncertainty and helps participants understand how value is created within the network. Greater transparency strengthens confidence in decentralized ecosystems.
Data should be treated as an asset that belongs to its creators. Decentralized AI allows contributors to share valuable information while receiving incentives for their participation. Instead of giving data away without recognition, users become active stakeholders in the growth of intelligent systems. This creates a more balanced relationship between technology platforms and their communities.
The demand for computing power continues to increase as AI models become more advanced. Decentralized infrastructure enables individuals and organizations to contribute unused hardware to global AI networks. These shared resources improve scalability while reducing dependence on centralized providers. Crypto incentives encourage continuous participation and help expand available computing capacity.
Governance is becoming just as important as technology itself. Decentralized AI networks allow communities to vote on upgrades, funding priorities, and ecosystem development. This collaborative approach ensures that decisions reflect the interests of participants instead of a single organization. Shared governance promotes long term sustainability and stronger engagement.
The combination of AI and decentralized finance introduces new forms of automation. Intelligent agents can analyze information, execute transactions, and interact with blockchain protocols without constant supervision. These capabilities improve efficiency while reducing manual processes across digital economies. Autonomous systems will continue to expand as blockchain infrastructure matures.
Interoperability is another key advantage of decentralized ecosystems @quipnetwork . Open standards make it easier for AI applications, blockchain networks, and digital assets to communicate with one another. This reduces fragmentation and encourages collaboration across different platforms. Connected ecosystems unlock greater innovation than isolated technologies ever could.
Decentralized AI and crypto are redefining how value is created and shared in the digital age. Instead of concentrating intelligence, ownership, and rewards within a few organizations, these technologies distribute opportunities across global communities. The result is a more open, transparent, and resilient innovation economy. As adoption accelerates, decentralized AI has the potential to become one of the strongest foundations of the future internet.

A qualidade da resposta depende diretamente da qualidade da pesquisa realizada e das informações disponíveis para fundamentá-la. No Direito, isso exige acesso a jurisprudência, legislação e doutrina, além de referências que permitam ao profissional conferir cada informação utilizada.
É para resolver esse problema que existe a IAJus. A plataforma disponibiliza uma base jurídica estruturada e rastreável, combinando diferentes modalidades de busca com uma ontologia própria baseada nas Tabelas Processuais Unificadas do Conselho Nacional de Justiça.
Os resultados apresentam referências e links para as fontes originais, permitindo sua verificação e reduzindo o risco de utilização de decisões, normas ou fundamentos inexistentes ou inadequados ao caso.
A IAJus pode ser utilizada pelo WhatsApp, por pesquisa via e-mail ou diretamente em ferramentas como ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, Gemini Spark, Perplexity, Grok, Manus, Mistral e outras plataformas compatíveis com plugins, conectores ou MCPs.
Assim, o profissional pode continuar utilizando a ferramenta de IA de sua preferência, mas com acesso a uma infraestrutura de pesquisa jurídica concebida para preservar a qualidade e a rastreabilidade dos resultados.

[curiouswavefn]So here's a great example of where we are with agentic AI: Instead of just being an assistant, it's behaving more like a collaborator and creative scientist.
In a recent project, I gave the system a molecular design problem typical of the problems we encounter in chemistry. Two similar molecules were giving very different results.
The AI proactively, autonomously, came up with four hypotheses and started testing them rigorously. Hypothesis 1 passed some initial tests and seemed promising. Hypothesis 2 looked promising, but a calculation turned up the opposite result, so it was rejected. Hypothesis 3 was inconclusive.
At this point, a human would be tempted to update their priors on Hypotheses 1 through elimination and prefer it as the favored one.

[HedgieMarkets]🦔AI companies are bulk-buying rare books, scanning them through high-speed machines that cut the spines off, and shredding the originals. A service called ISBNdb facilitates orders of up to a million books and keeps buyers anonymous. Pre-2022 books are premium because they're free of AI-generated text. A federal judge ruled the practice is fair use because eliminating the original means only one copy exists at a time. Anthropic hired the former head of Google Books partnerships to obtain "all the books in the world."
My Take This got to me. A bookseller told 404 Media that rare books with almost no surviving copies are being fed into this pipeline. Books that survived wars, fires, and centuries of handling are being shredded so an AI can learn to write a better marketing email. ISBNdb's website literally says "'AI company destroys two million books' is not a headline that generates sympathy," and they still built an entire business around making it happen quietly. They offer NDAs as a feature. They coach clients to call it "digital preservation."
I've covered AI companies scraping the internet, torrenting libraries, and stealing music. This is worse because it's irreversible. You can re-upload a website. You can reprint a bestseller. You can't replace the last three copies of an 18th-century botanical text once someone shreds them for training data. And the judge said it's legal. So it's going to accelerate. "We shred rare books and offer NDAs so nobody finds out" is a legitimate business model in 2026. What a timeline.
Hedgie🤗

[PrakamyaMishra]We are excited to introduce Instella-MoE✨, AMD's first fully open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model!
Instella-MoE has 16B total parameters with only 2.8B active parameters per token. Trained from scratch on AMD Instinct™ MI300X and MI325X GPUs using AMD-Primus and Miles frameworks, Instella-MoE combines a sparsely activated MoE design with architectural innovations such as Gated Multi-head Latent Attention (Gated MLA) and FarSkip-Collective. At its scale, it achieves state-of-the-art performance among fully open models.
💡 What makes this release especially significant is that we are opening up far more than the final model weights. The release provides the complete end-to-end training pipeline:
📚 Checkpoints across Pre-training → Mid-training → Long-context extension → SFT → DPO → RL ⚙️ Training recipes and configurations 🗂️ Data mixtures 💻 Training and inference code
We hope this release supports more transparent, reproducible, and efficient open LLM research. We’d love to hear your feedback.

[elonmusk]BREAKING: Europe is facing a historic birth collapse.
• EU: 3.46 million births vs 4.81 million deaths in 2025, a natural loss of 1.35 million people.
• 21 of 27 EU countries recorded more deaths than births. The EU’s population growth came entirely from migration.
• Fertility fell to a record-low 1.34 in 2024, declining in 24 of 27 member states.
• Germany: 654,241 births in 2025, the lowest postwar total. Fertility fell to 1.32.
• France: Fertility fell to 1.56, the lowest since WWI. Deaths exceeded births for the first time since WWII.
• Italy: Just 355,000 births vs 652,000 deaths. Fertility fell to 1.14.
• Poland: 238,000 births, the lowest postwar total. Deaths exceeded births by 168,000.
• Czechia: 77,636 births, the lowest ever. Fertility fell to 1.28.
• England and Wales: Births fell 1.6% in 2025, while fertility dropped to an estimated 1.39.
• Scotland: Births reached their lowest level since records began in 1855. Fertility hit a record-low 1.25.
• Austria: Births fell to a 25-year low. Fertility hit a record-low 1.30.
• Switzerland: Fertility fell again to 1.28 in 2025.
• Greece: 68,467 births vs 126,916 deaths.
• Malta, Spain and Lithuania recorded the EU’s lowest fertility rates: 1.01, 1.10 and 1.11.
• Spain still recorded 122,167 more deaths than births in 2025, despite a small rise in births.
• Finland: Fertility rose slightly to 1.30 in 2025, but remains far below 1.87 in 2010.
• Replacement level is roughly 2.1 children per woman.
• Europe’s demographic crisis is no longer limited to just a few countries.

The same force, showing up in different places
Take AI driven demand as an example. When enthusiasm and spending around artificial intelligence pick up, that energy doesn't stay contained to one sector. [thebuggeddev]Only if education could be this interactive ❤️‍🔥
I've had a looong wish to build something genuinely useful through vibe coding, and I finally did it.
A 3D human anatomy application built with @threejs using GPT 5.6 Sol.
It all started with a single design image that I created using GPT Image 2.0. I then used it to generate every 3D organ image, one by one.
Next, I converted each of those images into 3D models using @tripoai (and no, they didn't sponsor this 😄).
After that, I opened Codex, wrote a master prompt based on the design, and gave it the prompt, the design image, and all the 3D models.
Codex built the first version beautifully, but there was one big problem.
Every single 3D model was nearly 120-150 MB. That obviously wasn't practical for the web and was giving a performance of 16fps.
After a few iterations, Codex optimized each model down to roughly 2–5.5 MB while preserving the visual quality, reducing the total asset size from ~900 MB to just 28.6 MB. And each model loads on demand.
Along the way, Codex also generated those anatomical illustrations showing where each organ sits in the human body, and even created the interactive hotspot markers that explain different parts of every organ. It handled all of that.
The process wasn't exactly one shot, but it also wasn't difficult. You just have to do it step by step.
It genuinely felt like building something that could make learning anatomy much more engaging.
The inspiration came from @DilumSanjaya's 3D animal plant cell project. I remember seeing it and thinking, "I want to build something like this one day."
And I did it :D

[dr_cintas]if you use claude code, this will save you real money.
the problem: every time you make an edit, your ai rereads the whole codebase to figure out what changed. tens of thousands of tokens, every turn, for context it already had.
this repo fixes it. it’s called code review graph, and it just maps your entire codebase:
every file, every function, every connection laid out so you can see the actual shape of your project
how to set up (2 min):
1. pip install code-review-graph 2. code-review-graph install - auto-configures Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI + more 3. code-review-graph build
change one function, and it traces exactly what that touches... every caller, every dependent file, every test. your ai only reads what's affected, not the whole repo.
and the savings are wild. a task that used to burn ~100,000 tokens (about a dollar) now runs closer to a penny.
